cells.tense: The strength to keep going when it costs something is here and being used, and it waits on a choice not yet made.
cells.ask: Let the holding be enough on its own today — let one thing stay undecided and not reach for the next step to prove the strength is real — and what arrives is a steadiness that isn't straining toward anything.
cells.core:
You're standing on ground where nothing is decided yet, and you can carry weight without it bending you. There's no audience for this and no proof owed — the effort is private, and that's exactly what makes it solid. Nothing about the carrying needs to be shown to anyone. Something in you knows how to hold, and it's holding now.

The holding can rest here. Let one thing remain open a little past the point where you'd normally force it closed, and the strength shows itself as something that can wait, not just something that can push. A steadiness comes back that isn't straining toward anything.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding through the weight here, on ground that's still open, and it's working.
cells.verb: holding the line under material pressure — persisting through what the body must carry
cells.place: on the open ground before anything is chosen, where the whole of what could be is still undecided

cells.tense: Ahead of you is a version where everything is already decided and carried, and you're living as if you're in it.
cells.ask: Name one thing that hasn't happened yet and hand it back — let tomorrow hold it until tomorrow — and what returns is a load that lightens because it was never yours to carry today.
cells.core:
You're standing where nothing is fixed, and there's real strength available for whatever eventually gets chosen. Anyone carrying weight well here would do it without hurry, because the ground hasn't asked for a decision yet. The capacity to persist is genuine — it just has nothing to push against.

Yet you're insisting on the fixed version anyway. Every open door gets a conclusion slammed on it before anything can arrive, and the bracing is spending the strength it was meant to protect. One thing you've already taken as decided hasn't happened yet. Set it down and let it stay future — the load lightens because it was never yours to carry today.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying what hasn't arrived, and forcing decisions the ground hasn't made yet.
cells.verb: holding the line under material pressure — persisting through what the body must carry
cells.place: on the open ground before anything is chosen, where the whole of what could be is still undecided

cells.tense: You stopped at a door that's already behind you, and you're still standing there.
cells.ask: Say out loud what you've been holding privately, to one person who can see it — let the effort be witnessed without asking anyone to lift it — and what returns is a weight that loosens once it is not carried alone.
cells.core:
The strength to keep going is yours — you can feel it in how you stand, how you wait, how you don't fold. In a place where nothing is decided yet, that strength would be ready and unforced, willing to hold until the ground says which way.

It isn't moving right now. The weight is still there. The grip on it isn't — and you're standing where a choice was already made, holding still as if the ground might move. Nothing gets forced back by trying harder at the carrying. Put the effort where someone can see it — one person, one sentence about what you've been holding without telling anyone. The weight loosens once it is not carried alone.
cells.sheetLine: You have strength for the weight, and you've stopped putting it down and picking it up again.
cells.verb: holding the line under material pressure — persisting through what the body must carry
cells.place: on the open ground before anything is chosen, where the whole of what could be is still undecided

cells.tense: You're holding steady right now without giving it a name, as if the holding were happening to you.
cells.ask: Call one thing you've been doing today a choice you made — the simplest, most ordinary one — and what returns is the strength becoming yours to direct instead of something you're standing in.
cells.core:
You are steady. You keep going when things cost something, and you do it in the plain, unglamorous way — no announcement, no audience, just the weight carried. In a place where nothing is decided yet, that kind of steadiness is what lets possibility stay open without falling apart. Something in you knows how to hold, and it's holding now.

The carrying is happening without you saying so. You've been describing it as just how things are, as if the strength were something you stand in rather than something you do. Name one thing you've been doing today as a choice you made — the smallest, plainest one — and the strength becomes yours to direct instead of something you're standing in.
cells.sheetLine: You're carrying the weight already. You just haven't claimed it as yours.
cells.verb: holding the line under material pressure — persisting through what the body must carry
